text: For polynomials p_n of exact degree n on a real interval, orthogonality with respect to a nonnegative admissible weight w means the weighted integral of p_n p_m vanishes for n≠m; the DLMF also specifies discrete weights and a Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure generalization.

context: OpenStax Calculus 1 §4.10: the F+C uniqueness conclusion uses connected interval I; on disconnected domains constants on different components can differ. Indefinite integral notation represents a family, not a single numerical integral.
editorial_note: OpenStax Calculus 1 §4.10: the F+C uniqueness conclusion uses connected interval I; on disconnected domains constants on different components can differ. Indefinite integral notation represents a family, not a single numerical integral.
text: For a real-valued function f on an interval I, a differentiable F is an antiderivative of f if F'(x)=f(x) for all x∈I. The indefinite integral notation denotes the family F+C, with one constant C on a connected interval.

context: OpenStax Calculus 1 §2.5 assumes a full punctured interval. Relative-domain and one-sided versions need separate quantifier domains and accumulation-point/directional hypotheses; f(a) is irrelevant.
editorial_note: OpenStax Calculus 1 §2.5 assumes a full punctured interval. Relative-domain and one-sided versions need separate quantifier domains and accumulation-point/directional hypotheses; f(a) is irrelevant.
text: Assume f is defined on a punctured interval around a∈R. A finite real limit L exists at a if every ε>0 admits δ>0 such that 0<|x−a|<δ implies |f(x)−L|<ε.
